Judt's exploration of postwar Europe is a fascinating examination of the events, people and culture that emerged after World War II. The book is at its best when examining the cultural changes that occurred in the European countries post war and the rise and fall of communism. It dispatches many of the immediate post-war myths about communist Europe and brings a slightly new perspective to that era.
